newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sets 25 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sets 25 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.

text.p: The Central Bank of Venezuela announced for Wednesday morning a 15 billion bolivar ($32 million) auction of 180-day "monetary stabilization," or TEM, bills with a 21.99 percent coupon.
The bank said it would also offer five billion bolivars ($11 million) in 269-day bills with a 22.57 percent coupon, and another five billion bolivars of 359-day bills with a 23.19 percent coupon.
No TEMs are maturing this week.

Coupons are also up from last week's 35 billion bolivar issue when 179-, 269- and 358-day notes carried 21.62, 22.20 and 22.79 percent coupons respectively for effective yields of 21.98, 25.60 and 27.23 percent.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
